previous_statement: Theorem 1.2 (Efficient pure state tomography): Given n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon) copies of |psi> in C^d, algorithm A_GKKT outputs |v> with |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon w.p. >= 1-delta, using unentangled measurements in poly(n) time. Proof: Set q = epsilon/2 in Lemma 4.2. With n = C(d + log(1/delta))/epsilon^2 * epsilon = C(d + log(1/delta))/epsilon, the failure probability is <= delta. Since ||rho_hat_avg - |psi><psi|||_infty <= epsilon/2, the top eigenvector |v> of rho_hat_avg satisfies |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1 - 2*||rho_hat_avg - |psi><psi|||_infty >= 1-epsilon (by Mirsky/Weyl perturbation [HJ13]) and F(|psi><psi|, |v><v|) = |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon. Gate count: poly(n) from the t-design circuits and classical postprocessing.
new_statement: Theorem 1.2 (Efficient pure state tomography): Given n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon) copies of |psi> in C^d, algorithm A_GKKT outputs |v> with |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon w.p. >= 1-delta, using unentangled measurements in poly(n) time. Proof: Set q = sqrt(epsilon) in Lemma 4.2. The exponent becomes (4 log 3)d - n*epsilon/704. With n = C(d + log(1/delta))/epsilon for C = 704*5 (say), the failure probability is at most 2*exp(-4*log(1/delta)) <= delta. Conditioned on success, ||rho_hat_avg - |psi><psi|||_infty <= sqrt(epsilon). The fidelity argument proceeds in several steps: (a) By Mirsky's inequality [HJ13, Cor. 7.4.9.3], the eigenvalues of rho_hat_avg are within sqrt(epsilon) of those of |psi><psi| (which are 1,0,...,0), so the top eigenvalue satisfies lambda_1 >= 1-sqrt(epsilon) and all others <= sqrt(epsilon). (b) The top eigenvector |v> satisfies ||v><v| - |psi><psi|||_infty <= 2*sqrt(epsilon) by the Davis-Kahan sin(theta) theorem. (c) Converting to trace distance: ||v><v| - |psi><psi|||_1 <= 2*sqrt(2*sqrt(epsilon)) (since ||A||_1 <= sqrt(rank(A))*||A||_F and rank <= 2). (d) For pure states, |<v|psi>|^2 = 1 - (||v><v| - |psi><psi|||_1/2)^2 >= 1 - 4*sqrt(epsilon) [Wat18, Eq. 1.186]. (e) Replacing epsilon by epsilon^2/16 gives |<v|psi>|^2 >= 1-epsilon with n = O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon). Gate count: poly(n) from the t-design circuits (Theorem 4.1) and classical eigenvalue computation.
